reasoningSteps: FIRST describes EPSS as the probability that a published CVE will be exploited in the wild in the next 30 days. It publishes probability values from 0 to 1 along with ranking percentiles.
A synthetic record with probability 0.08 and percentile 0.97 means an 8 percent predicted exploitation probability and a high relative rank, not a 97 percent exploitation probability.
The percentile describes position relative to other scores. It is not an additional event probability to multiply by 0.08 or a replacement for that probability.
EPSS does not, by itself, give the probability that a particular local host will be compromised or the monetary impact on that host.
Record score date, prediction horizon and applicability alongside severity and local context. These example numbers are invented and are not a current score for any real CVE.

reasoningSteps: Suppose two controls each fail with marginal probability 0.10 in a synthetic scenario, and the modeled bad outcome occurs only if both fail.

If the two failures always occur together because of a shared cause, the same marginal failure rates yield joint failure probability 0.10, not 0.01.
The marginal rates alone do not determine the joint rate. With both marginals 0.10, a feasible joint rate can range from 0 to 0.10; disjoint failures give the lower endpoint.

A product is therefore conditional on the modeled dependence structure. Shared credentials, power or administrative paths may undermine an independence assumption; this example does not assess any real control system.
